scope: All 108 names: the text was compared name by name with the page images of the TTD book (pp. 33–35), and every meaning was read against its name. There are no word-by-word glosses on this page (the meanings are per name). The range-number flags are the block labels. One spelling (mathurā-/madhurā-, name 57) could not be made out at the scan's resolution. The same 108 names stand inside the Satyanārāyaṇa page from a different book, with a few different readings; they were not harmonised.

items.issue: Name 11 ended -śaṅkhādyudāyudhāya (the usual reading); the print has -śaṅkhādyāyudhāya, which is what the meaning already translated.
Small departures from the print: ilāpataye (print iḷā-), vṛndāvanāntasañcāriṇe (print bṛndāvanāntassañcāriṇe), paramapūruṣāya (print -puruṣāya), kālīya- (print kāḷīya-).
Name 64, kubjākṛṣṭāmbaradharāya, was “wearing the garment Kubjā brought”; ākṛṣṭa is “pulled”: Kubjā tugged at his upper cloth (Bhāgavata 10.42).
